segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Thirty-Nine. Equal triangles on the same base and on the same side lie in the same parallels. Let triangles A B C and D B C be equal in area, standing on the same base B C and on the same side of it. We prove that the segment A D joining their vertices is parallel to base B C.

segments.text: Join point A to point D with segment A D. Suppose segment A D is not parallel to segment B C. Then by Proposition Thirty-One, through point A draw segment A E parallel to segment B C, meeting segment B D at point E, and join point E to point C.

segments.text: Since triangles A B C and E B C stand on the same base B C and lie in the same parallels B C and A E, by Proposition Thirty-Seven, triangle A B C equals triangle E B C. Yet by hypothesis, triangle A B C equals triangle D B C. By Common Notion One, things equal to the same thing are equal to one another, so triangle D B C equals triangle E B C, the greater equal to the less, which is impossible. Thus segment A E cannot be parallel to segment B C, nor can any other line through point A except segment A D. Therefore segment A D is parallel to segment B C, as was required to prove.
